findings.claim: Audio signals and AC mains are sine waves.
findings.truth: A sine wave represents a single-frequency pure tone. Audio signals can contain many frequencies, so they are not generally sine waves.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia Audio signal and Sine wave pages fetched

findings.claim: The specification requires a minimum of two input signals. Up to four inputs may be used.
findings.truth: The specification requires learners to analyse mixer circuits based on a summing op-amp but gives no four-input maximum. A summing amplifier can combine two or more inputs.
findings.evidence: spec 2.2 Operational amplifiers; Wikipedia Operational amplifier applications, summing amplifier section, fetched

findings.claim: The maximum number of inputs a summing amplifier may have in this specification is Four.
findings.truth: The specification sets no maximum number of summing-amplifier inputs.
findings.evidence: spec 2.2 Operational amplifiers; Wikipedia Operational amplifier applications, summing amplifier section, fetched

findings.claim: The question excludes changing C but its supplied answer says to use a larger capacitor.
findings.truth: For T = 1.1RC, increasing C allows the same delay with a smaller R. The question must permit a change to C for its supplied answer to be valid.

findings.claim: Mark-space ratio equals the duty cycle above 50%.
findings.truth: Mark-space ratio is mark time divided by space time. In a standard 555 astable it is greater than 1, so the duty cycle is above 50%; the two quantities are not equal.

findings.claim: A rising-edge-triggered 2-bit up-counter clocks the second flip-flop from Q0 and then sequences 00, 01, 10, 11.
findings.truth: With rising-edge-triggered D flip-flops configured to toggle, clocking the second stage from Q0 gives a down sequence. Clock it from Q-bar of the first stage, so the second stage clocks when Q0 falls, to obtain the stated up sequence.
findings.evidence: spec 2.2 Sequential systems; Nexperia 74HC74 datasheet (positive-edge triggering), fetched; Wikipedia Counter (digital), fetched

findings.claim: A decoder/driver is described as converting a 4017 counter output to a 7-segment display.
findings.truth: The specification's decimal-display system is a 4-bit BCD counter, decoder/driver and 7-segment display. The 4017 is specified separately as a sequencer, so the decoder question must name a BCD counter.

findings.claim: Any noise signal smaller than the hysteresis band cannot cause a false triggering event.
findings.truth: Hysteresis prevents repeated switching: after one threshold is crossed, the input must cross the other threshold for another transition. Whether one noise pulse causes a transition also depends on the input's starting voltage.
findings.evidence: Nexperia 74HC14 datasheet, hysteresis transfer characteristics, fetched; Wikipedia Schmitt trigger, noise-immunity section, fetched

findings.claim: Every flowchart uses exactly four standard block types and must start and end with a terminator.
findings.truth: The four blocks are useful common blocks for this lesson, but standard flowcharts have other symbols. A program that loops indefinitely has no End terminator.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia Flowchart, common symbols and other symbols sections, fetched; spec 2.2 Control circuits requires flowchart design and analysis without prescribing four exclusive blocks

findings.claim: An analogue sensor cannot be connected directly to a microcontroller input pin without an interface circuit.
findings.truth: An analogue signal can be read by an analogue-to-digital converter. A digital-only input needs a conditioning interface that produces a valid logic signal.
findings.evidence: lesson 9 content_html correctly distinguishes a Schmitt/comparator interface from an ADC input; spec 2.2 Control circuits requires interfacing sensing circuits

findings.claim: Four named vehicle examples and four named reasons are presented as specification-prescribed examinable lists.
findings.truth: The specification requires applications and reasons for adopting microcontrollers in vehicle and domestic-appliance industries, but it does not prescribe either named list.

findings.claim: Both resistors must be at least 1 kΩ in any op-amp circuit design.
findings.truth: Option A: retain it only if a board source establishes a task-specific minimum. Option B: remove the universal rule; the specification requires resistor selection for a given gain but states no universal 1 kΩ minimum. Recommendation: use option B unless a board source is supplied.
findings.evidence: spec 2.2 Operational amplifiers; no board source for the claimed universal minimum was available

summary: Verified fixes address waveform terminology, summing inputs, timing, counter design, display interfacing, hysteresis and flowchart claims. One unsupported universal op-amp-resistor rule requires adjudication.
